!76 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// What to look for: the ray payload size the issue asks for is already in the\0A// compiler's own output, in the dx.entryPoints named metadata at the bottom of\0A// the DXIL pane. Each entry there is a list of tag/value pairs. Tag 8 is the\0A// shader kind (7 raygeneration, 8 intersection, 9 anyhit, 10 closesthit,\0A// 11 miss, 12 callable), tag 6 is the ray payload size in bytes, and tag 7 is\0A// the intersection attribute size in bytes. This shader declares a 28-byte\0A// payload, an 8-byte attribute struct and a 12-byte callable parameter, so the\0A// anyhit and closesthit entries carry 28 and 8, the miss entry carries 28, and\0A// the callable entry carries 12. The raygeneration and intersection entries\0A// carry neither, because neither takes a payload. The same three values are\0A// also written into the container's RDAT part as PayloadSizeInBytes,\0A// AttributeSizeInBytes and ShaderKind.\0A//\0A// What Compiler Explorer cannot show is the actual subject of the issue. There\0A// is no way to call a reflection interface from here, so the finding that\0A// ID3D12FunctionReflection exposes the shader kind but has no field that can\0A// hold the payload size comes from a purpose-built harness recorded in the\0A// triage notes, not from this pane. Treat this link as evidence that the data\0A// exists and has existed in every release, not as evidence about the API.\0A//\0A// Both panes are expected to compile cleanly and to agree. That is the point:\0A// this is a feature request about API surface, not a bug, and nothing here\0A// changed between the oldest compiler Compiler Explorer offers and trunk.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// #2952 -- \22Expose ray payload size / function type through Reflection\22\0A//\0A// Agent-constructed. The issue has no repro: it asks whether the payload size\0A// and the shader kind (\22raygen, miss...\22) of a DXR library entry can be\0A// retrieved from a reflection container. So this library declares one function\0A// of every DXR 1.0 shader kind, plus a plain (non-entry) library function, and\0A// gives each size a value that cannot be confused with any other number in the\0A// reflection output:\0A//\0A//   RayPayload      float4 + float3            = 28 bytes\0A//   Attributes      BuiltInTriangleIntersectionAttributes (float2) = 8 bytes\0A//   CallableParams  float2 + uint              = 12 bytes\0A//\0A// 28, 8 and 12 are all distinct from the resource and constant-buffer counts\0A// this library produces, so \22the API reported the payload size\22 cannot be\0A// satisfied by coincidence.\0A//\0A// lib_6_3 is the oldest library profile in the release sequence and is DXR\0A// 1.0, per SKILL.md's \22target the repro at the oldest profile that still shows\0A// the symptom\22.\0A\0Astruct RayPayload {\0A  float4 color;\0A  float3 hitPoint;\0A};\0A\0Astruct CallableParams {\0A  float2 uv;\0A  uint id;\0A};\0A\0ARaytracingAccelerationStructure Scene : register(t0);\0ARWTexture2D<float4> Output : register(u0);\0A\0A[shader(\22raygeneration\22)] void RayGenMain() {\0A  RayPayload payload;\0A  payload.color = float4(0, 0, 0, 0);\0A  payload.hitPoint = float3(0, 0, 0);\0A\0A  RayDesc ray;\0A  ray.Origin = float3(0, 0, 0);\0A  ray.Direction = float3(0, 0, 1);\0A  ray.TMin = 0.001;\0A  ray.TMax = 10000.0;\0A\0A  TraceRay(Scene, RAY_FLAG_NONE, 0xFF, 0, 1, 0, ray, payload);\0A  Output[DispatchRaysIndex().xy] = payload.color;\0A}\0A\0A[shader(\22miss\22)] void MissMain(inout RayPayload payload) {\0A  payload.color = float4(0, 0, 1, 1);\0A}\0A\0A[shader(\22closesthit\22)] void ClosestHitMain(\0A    inout RayPayload payload, in BuiltInTriangleIntersectionAttributes attr) {\0A  payload.color = float4(attr.barycentrics, 0, 1);\0A  payload.hitPoint = WorldRayOrigin() + RayTCurrent() * WorldRayDirection();\0A}\0A\0A[shader(\22anyhit\22)] void AnyHitMain(\0A    inout RayPayload payload, in BuiltInTriangleIntersectionAttributes attr) {\0A  if (attr.barycentrics.x < 0.01)\0A    IgnoreHit();\0A}\0A\0A[shader(\22intersection\22)] void IntersectionMain() {\0A  BuiltInTriangleIntersectionAttributes attr;\0A  attr.barycentrics = float2(0.25, 0.25);\0A  ReportHit(1.0, 0, attr);\0A}\0A\0A[shader(\22callable\22)] void CallableMain(inout CallableParams params) {\0A  params.uv = params.uv * 2.0;\0A  params.id = params.id + 1;\0A}\0A\0A// A plain library function, not an entry point: its reflected shader kind\0A// should be Library, which is what distinguishes \22the kind field is populated\22\0A// from \22the kind field happens to hold a constant\22.\0Aexport float3 PlainLibraryFunction(float3 v) { return v * 2.0f; }\0A"}

!75 = !{!"dxc(private) 1.9.0.10001 (main, beb6c47d)"}
!76 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// What to look for: the ray payload size the issue asks for is already in the\0A// compiler's own output, in the dx.entryPoints named metadata at the bottom of\0A// the DXIL pane. Each entry there is a list of tag/value pairs. Tag 8 is the\0A// shader kind (7 raygeneration, 8 intersection, 9 anyhit, 10 closesthit,\0A// 11 miss, 12 callable), tag 6 is the ray payload size in bytes, and tag 7 is\0A// the intersection attribute size in bytes. This shader declares a 28-byte\0A// payload, an 8-byte attribute struct and a 12-byte callable parameter, so the\0A// anyhit and closesthit entries carry 28 and 8, the miss entry carries 28, and\0A// the callable entry carries 12. The raygeneration and intersection entries\0A// carry neither, because neither takes a payload. The same three values are\0A// also written into the container's RDAT part as PayloadSizeInBytes,\0A// AttributeSizeInBytes and ShaderKind.\0A//\0A// What Compiler Explorer cannot show is the actual subject of the issue. There\0A// is no way to call a reflection interface from here, so the finding that\0A// ID3D12FunctionReflection exposes the shader kind but has no field that can\0A// hold the payload size comes from a purpose-built harness recorded in the\0A// triage notes, not from this pane. Treat this link as evidence that the data\0A// exists and has existed in every release, not as evidence about the API.\0A//\0A// Both panes are expected to compile cleanly and to agree. That is the point:\0A// this is a feature request about API surface, not a bug, and nothing here\0A// changed between the oldest compiler Compiler Explorer offers and trunk.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// #2952 -- \22Expose ray payload size / function type through Reflection\22\0A//\0A// Agent-constructed. The issue has no repro: it asks whether the payload size\0A// and the shader kind (\22raygen, miss...\22) of a DXR library entry can be\0A// retrieved from a reflection container. So this library declares one function\0A// of every DXR 1.0 shader kind, plus a plain (non-entry) library function, and\0A// gives each size a value that cannot be confused with any other number in the\0A// reflection output:\0A//\0A//   RayPayload      float4 + float3            = 28 bytes\0A//   Attributes      BuiltInTriangleIntersectionAttributes (float2) = 8 bytes\0A//   CallableParams  float2 + uint              = 12 bytes\0A//\0A// 28, 8 and 12 are all distinct from the resource and constant-buffer counts\0A// this library produces, so \22the API reported the payload size\22 cannot be\0A// satisfied by coincidence.\0A//\0A// lib_6_3 is the oldest library profile in the release sequence and is DXR\0A// 1.0, per SKILL.md's \22target the repro at the oldest profile that still shows\0A// the symptom\22.\0A\0Astruct RayPayload {\0A  float4 color;\0A  float3 hitPoint;\0A};\0A\0Astruct CallableParams {\0A  float2 uv;\0A  uint id;\0A};\0A\0ARaytracingAccelerationStructure Scene : register(t0);\0ARWTexture2D<float4> Output : register(u0);\0A\0A[shader(\22raygeneration\22)] void RayGenMain() {\0A  RayPayload payload;\0A  payload.color = float4(0, 0, 0, 0);\0A  payload.hitPoint = float3(0, 0, 0);\0A\0A  RayDesc ray;\0A  ray.Origin = float3(0, 0, 0);\0A  ray.Direction = float3(0, 0, 1);\0A  ray.TMin = 0.001;\0A  ray.TMax = 10000.0;\0A\0A  TraceRay(Scene, RAY_FLAG_NONE, 0xFF, 0, 1, 0, ray, payload);\0A  Output[DispatchRaysIndex().xy] = payload.color;\0A}\0A\0A[shader(\22miss\22)] void MissMain(inout RayPayload payload) {\0A  payload.color = float4(0, 0, 1, 1);\0A}\0A\0A[shader(\22closesthit\22)] void ClosestHitMain(\0A    inout RayPayload payload, in BuiltInTriangleIntersectionAttributes attr) {\0A  payload.color = float4(attr.barycentrics, 0, 1);\0A  payload.hitPoint = WorldRayOrigin() + RayTCurrent() * WorldRayDirection();\0A}\0A\0A[shader(\22anyhit\22)] void AnyHitMain(\0A    inout RayPayload payload, in BuiltInTriangleIntersectionAttributes attr) {\0A  if (attr.barycentrics.x < 0.01)\0A    IgnoreHit();\0A}\0A\0A[shader(\22intersection\22)] void IntersectionMain() {\0A  BuiltInTriangleIntersectionAttributes attr;\0A  attr.barycentrics = float2(0.25, 0.25);\0A  ReportHit(1.0, 0, attr);\0A}\0A\0A[shader(\22callable\22)] void CallableMain(inout CallableParams params) {\0A  params.uv = params.uv * 2.0;\0A  params.id = params.id + 1;\0A}\0A\0A// A plain library function, not an entry point: its reflected shader kind\0A// should be Library, which is what distinguishes \22the kind field is populated\22\0A// from \22the kind field happens to hold a constant\22.\0Aexport float3 PlainLibraryFunction(float3 v) { return v * 2.0f; }\0A"}
